blocks.content: A volume's access mode defines how many nodes can mount it, and whether they can write to it, a real constraint that trips up a lot of people designing multi-replica applications.

ReadWriteOnce (RWO) means the volume can be mounted read-write by exactly one node at a time, this is the most common access mode, and the one most cloud block storage (like AWS EBS or GCP Persistent Disk) actually supports.

blocks.alt: Read-write, but from exactly one node at a time

blocks.content: ReadOnlyMany (ROX) allows many nodes to mount the same volume simultaneously, but only for reading, no node can write to it, a fit for shared, static reference data multiple Pods across different nodes all need to read.

blocks.alt: Shared read access across many nodes, with no writing allowed at all

blocks.content: ReadWriteMany (RWX) allows many nodes to mount and write to the same volume simultaneously, genuinely useful, but it requires a storage backend specifically built to support concurrent writers, ordinary cloud block storage typically cannot do this at all.

blocks.alt: Concurrent read-write from many nodes, a real backend requirement, not universal

blocks.content:
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany   # only works if the underlying storage backend actually supports it

spec:

blocks.content: This trips people up constantly: a Deployment with several replicas spread across different nodes, all trying to share one PVC, needs ReadWriteMany, if the storage backend only supports RWO (very common on cloud block storage), that design simply will not work, and needs rethinking, often toward per-replica storage instead.

blocks.alt: A very common design mistake, worth knowing about before it happens

blocks.content: A newer mode, ReadWriteOncePod, restricts a volume to being mounted read-write by a single specific Pod, not just a single node, a genuinely tighter guarantee for cases where even two Pods on the same node should never share write access.

blocks.alt: An even tighter guarantee, scoped to one specific Pod, not just one node

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Access modes (RWO, ROX, RWX, and the newer RWOP) define how many nodes, or even Pods, can mount a volume and whether they can write to it, real constraints, not formalities.
A common real mistake is designing a multi-replica app around shared storage that needs RWX when the underlying backend only supports RWO, worth checking early.
